# BakeNN 0.1.0

The first alpha release of BakeNN turns a trained FP32 PyTorch model and
representative calibration data into a fixed-shape INT8 execution plan and a
standalone, heap-free C11 firmware library.

Highlights:

- typed quantized IR, static liveness/SRAM planning and compile-time budgets;
- versioned byte-exact `bakenn.int8.v1` Python/C numerical contract;
- Conv/Depthwise/Linear, residual/SE, pooling, shape, resize, grouped
  ConvTranspose and compact vision/audio model coverage;
- direct pinned CMSIS-NN and ESP-NN source backends with portable C fallback;
- self-contained Cortex-M, RV32IMC and ESP-IDF target artifacts;
- deterministic text/JSON memory reports and physical benchmark evidence.

On the checked-in original-ESP32 MobileNetV2-0.25 measurement, direct
BakeNN-to-ESP-NN execution produced the same INT8 output as TFLM+ESP-NN, used
1.22% lower median latency, a 30.1% smaller app binary and 66.5% less linked
DRAM.  The nRF52840 direct-CMSIS-NN FC measurement used 30.1% fewer cycles,
70.0% less linked Flash and 22.6% less linked static SRAM than TFLM using the
same CMSIS-NN FC family.  These results are scoped to their frozen models,
boards and toolchains; see the attached evidence archive and
`benchmarks/RESULTS.md` for the exact contracts and limitations.

This is alpha software with intentional static batch-one, fixed-shape and
single-public-input/output constraints.  Read `STABILITY.md` before depending
on generated ABI details.
